chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a boy who had not reached maturity and a woman who killed a man, so he said:

Indeed, the mistake of the woman and the boy is treated as intentional. So if the heirs of the slain wish to kill both of them, they may kill them both, and they return five thousand dirhams to the boy’s heirs. And if they wish to kill the boy, they may kill him, and the woman returns a quarter of the blood money to the boy’s heirs.
He said: And if the heirs of the slain wish to kill the woman, they may kill her, and the boy returns a quarter of the blood money to the woman’s heirs.
He said: And if the heirs of the slain wish to take the blood money, then half of the blood money is upon the boy and half of the blood money is upon the woman.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ لَمْ يُدْرِكْ: a boy who has not yet reached maturity
key_terms.خَطَأَ الْمَرْأَةِ وَالْغُلَامِ عَمْدٌ: their mistaken killing is treated legally as intentional in this ruling
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: five thousand dirhams paid as compensation adjustment
key_terms.رُبُعَ الدِّيَةِ: a quarter of the prescribed blood money

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a non-mature boy and a woman jointly kill a man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a boy who has not reached maturity and a woman when they jointly kill a man. It outlines the options of qisas or diyyah for the heirs of the victim and specifies the financial adjustments owed between the parties’ heirs in each case.
